questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code cleans up when a step of provisioning fails? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The mailer raises an exception inside send_invite. Which cleanup happens, and in what order?
choices: Only the user is deleted, because the directory removes memberships with it
Recovery codes are revoked, then the user leaves each group in reverse order, then the user is deleted; the mailer error then propagates to the caller
The user is deleted first, then groups, then codes, and the mailer error is swallowed
Nothing is undone, because commit() has not been reached and the stack is discarded

questions.prompt: During rollback, delete_user itself raises an exception. What is the outcome?
choices: The rollback exception replaces the original error, which is lost
Remaining undo steps are skipped, because the first failure aborts the loop
The failure is logged, the other steps still run, and the original error propagates with a note naming the step that needs manual cleanup
The failure is silently ignored and the caller cannot tell cleanup was incomplete

questions.prompt: Why is the audit.record call placed after the with block instead of inside it?
choices: Because context managers cannot contain calls to external services
Because an audit failure inside the block would roll back an account that was already fully created and invited, whereas outside it only gets logged
Because the audit record must be written after the stack is garbage collected
Because inside the block the exception would be suppressed by __exit__
